easy.def: A big amount of something.
examples: I do not have much milk.
How much is it?
Too much sun can burn you.

more.def: A large amount of something that cannot be counted.
examples: There was not much snow, so we could not go sledding.
How much water does a camel drink?
We did not have much time to finish the test.

easy.def: A lot.
examples: I like it very much.
Thank you very much.
She did not sleep much.

more.def: To a great degree, or often.
examples: I miss my old school very much.
The baby does not cry much at night.
Her room is much bigger than mine.

easy.def: Wet, soft dirt.
examples: The pig rolled in the mud.
I stepped in mud.
My boots are covered in mud.

more.def: Soft, wet earth that is sticky.
examples: Heavy rain turned the field into thick mud.
My boots were covered in mud after the rain.
Kids made pies out of mud.

easy.def: A small, round cake that you eat at breakfast.
examples: I ate a muffin.
The muffin is warm.
The muffin has blueberries.

more.def: A small, round, sweet bread or cake that is baked in a cup.
examples: I ate a blueberry muffin for breakfast.
The muffins were still warm from the oven.
She split the muffin and spread butter on it.

easy.def: A big cup with a handle.
examples: I drink from a mug.
The mug is hot.
Mom filled the mug.

more.def: A large, round cup with a handle, used for hot drinks.
examples: I drank hot chocolate from a mug.
The mug had a picture of a cat.
Dad filled his mug with tea.

easy.def: A strong animal that is part horse and part donkey.
examples: The mule carried a load.
A mule is strong.
The mule pulled the cart.

more.def: An animal whose parents are a donkey and a horse, known for being strong and stubborn.
examples: The mule carried supplies up the trail.
A mule can be very stubborn.
The farmer used a mule to pull the plow.

easy.def: More than one.
examples: There are multiple choices.
The room has multiple doors.
The box has multiple parts.

more.def: Having or involving many parts or more than one.
examples: The test has multiple choices.
The building has multiple floors.
The movie has multiple endings.

easy.def: A number you get by multiplying.
examples: Ten is a multiple of five.
Six is a multiple of three.
The multiples of two are even.

more.def: A number that can be divided evenly by a smaller number.
examples: Eight is a multiple of four.
The multiples of three are three, six, nine and twelve.
Twenty is a multiple of both four and five.

easy.def: A word for mother.
examples: My mum made lunch.
I love my mum.
Mum read me a story.

more.def: A word that some people use for mother, mostly in Britain.
examples: My cousin in England calls his mother mum.
Mum packed sandwiches for the picnic.
Her mum waved from the window.

easy.def: A body wrapped in cloth that was kept safe in ancient Egypt.
examples: The mummy is in the museum.
A mummy is old.
We saw a mummy.

more.def: A dead body that was wrapped in cloth to keep it from rotting, as in ancient Egypt.
examples: We saw an Egyptian mummy at the museum.
The mummy was wrapped in strips of cloth.
The mummies were buried in tombs.

easy.def: A word some children use for mother.
examples: I love my mummy.
Mummy read me a story.
Mummy is home.

more.def: A word that some children use for their mother.
examples: My mummy tucked me in.
The little girl hugged her mummy.
Mummy packed a snack.

easy.def: A part of your body that helps you move.
examples: I have strong muscles.
Exercise makes your muscles grow.
My muscle hurts.

more.def: A part of the body made of tissue that tightens and relaxes to make you move.
examples: Your leg muscles help you run and jump.
Lifting weights makes your muscles stronger.
The heart is a muscle that pumps blood.

easy.def: A place where you can look at old or special things.
examples: We saw old bones at the museum.
The museum has old trains.
We saw art at the museum.

more.def: A building where interesting objects of art, history, or science are kept and shown.
examples: The museum has a real rocket hanging from the ceiling.
The science museum lets you touch the displays.
The town's museum tells the story of its first settlers.

easy.def: Sounds that people sing or play.
examples: I like music.
The music was loud.
We make music in class.

more.def: Sounds put together in a pleasing way, made by voices or instruments.
examples: She plays music on her violin every evening.
Music filled the room as the band began.
My favorite music has a fast beat.

easy.def: Having to do with music.
examples: She plays a musical instrument.
A piano is a musical instrument.
He has a musical talent.

more.def: Having to do with music, or good at music.
examples: A violin is a musical instrument.
She comes from a musical family.
He has a musical ear and can sing any song.

easy.def: A play or movie with songs.
examples: We saw a musical.
The musical had singing.
She was in the school musical.

more.def: A play or film in which the actors sing and dance as part of the story.
examples: We saw a musical about a wizard.
The school put on a musical this spring.
The actors in the musical sang and danced.

easy.def: A person who plays music.
examples: The musician plays the violin.
A musician sang.
She is a musician.

more.def: A person who plays an instrument or sings as a job or hobby.
examples: The musician played the violin.
Several musicians played in the park.
My aunt is a musician in an orchestra.

easy.def: A word used to say you have to do something.
examples: I must go home.
You must wear a helmet.
We must be quiet.

more.def: A word used to say that something is needed or required, or that something is very likely.
examples: You must wear a seat belt when you ride in a car.
She must be tired after the long hike.
All visitors must sign in at the front desk.

easy.def: A yellow sauce for sandwiches.
examples: I put mustard on my hot dog.
The mustard is yellow.
I like mustard.

more.def: A yellow or brown sauce with a sharp taste that is put on foods such as hot dogs.
examples: I put mustard on my sandwich.
The mustard was yellow and tangy.
Dad squeezed mustard onto the pretzel.

easy.def: Shared by two or more.
examples: We have a mutual friend.
The feeling was mutual.
We reached a mutual agreement.

more.def: Felt or done by each of two or more people toward the others.
examples: We have a mutual friend named Sam.
Their respect for each other was mutual.
The two teams had a mutual agreement.
